title: Scheduled machine maintenance
summary: Scheduled Temp clean-up, transcript retention, a boot-time record and an off-machine backup, all started hidden.
why: Machines slow down from the things nobody watches: Temp file counts, transcripts that pile up, backups that never happen. Small scheduled jobs keep each one bounded and measured.

items.title: Temp clean-up every 4 hours
items.does: Installs Temp-Hygiene.ps1 and a hidden task every 4 hours that removes stale scratch folders from Temp; locked folders are refused, the live session folder is never touched.
items.why: Temp file count is boot time: about 0.2 ms per file at logon, so 747,000 files once meant a boot of almost three minutes.
items.notes: Scratch is unlinked (it is regenerable); nothing else is touched.

items.title: Weekly transcript retention
items.does: Installs Clean-ClaudeTranscripts.ps1 and a weekly task (Sunday 04:30) that sends transcripts past the measured retention to the Recycle Bin.
items.why: Transcript folders grow without limit. The retention days are proposed from your own age histogram: a round-number guess once would have removed nothing at all.

items.title: Boot time record
items.does: Installs Record-BootTime.ps1 and a task at boot plus 3 minutes that appends this boot's logon timings and Temp counts to a CSV.
items.why: The built-in boot-duration event is missing on some machines, and a trend you do not record cannot be seen.

items.title: Daily off-machine git backup
items.does: Installs offsite_backup.py and a daily task (05:00) that sends an incremental git bundle to your backup machine over ssh and verifies the copy.
items.why: Without shadow copies on the machine, a force-push or a deleted branch is only recoverable from a copy somewhere else.
items.notes: Off unless you have a second machine; its ssh alias is asked in the wizard.

items.title: Wake-on-LAN sender
items.does: Installs wol.py, which wakes the backup machine with a magic packet and waits for ssh to answer.
items.why: The backup machine can stay switched off until a backup needs it.

items.title: Console health check
items.does: Uses the console's Health button: fixed-id checks for Temp, disk, boot, tasks, drift, worktrees, git objects and progress files.
items.why: One button that answers whether the machine is healthy saves a dozen ad hoc probes.
items.notes: Built into the console; this item only records that you want it.

items.title: Scheduled health check
items.does: Runs the console's delete-free health checks on a schedule and leaves a result file and one status line.
items.why: A problem found at 3 a.m. by a schedule is waiting for you at breakfast instead of surprising you at noon.
items.notes: Registered from the console's Health panel, which backs up and reads back the task.

items.title: Temp census
items.does: Installs temp_census.py, a read-only count of Temp files and sizes per name prefix.
items.why: It tells you which program fills Temp without waiting for the next clean-up run to find out.

items.title: Hidden task launcher
items.does: Installs Run-Hidden.vbs, which starts a PowerShell script from a scheduled task without a console window and passes its exit code back.
items.why: PowerShell 5.1 flashes a console window before it can hide itself; closing that window once killed the task it belonged to.

items.title: Task result codes that are not failures
items.does: Adds the fact that scheduled-task results 267009, 267011 and 2147946720 mean running, never run and already running.
items.why: Those three codes were reported as failures again and again; writing them down once ended it.

items.title: Runtime scripts are live
items.does: Adds the rule that scripts run by scheduled tasks are live: copy before editing and parse-check before walking away.
items.why: There is no deploy step between the file and the task, so a syntax error becomes a silently dead task.
